slides.text:
Go has first-class functions. A function is a value: you can keep it in a variable, pass it or return it.

Its **function type** is its shape, the parameter and result types with no name. The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
slides.code:
add    has type  func(int, int) int
halve  has type  func(int) int

slides.text:
A **function literal**, also called an anonymous function, has no name. Inside a function it is the only way to write one.

Put `(args)` right after its closing brace and it runs on the spot. That is an **IIFE**, an immediately invoked function expression. The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.

exercises.title: Function literals
exercises.guide: Store a function literal in a variable, then replace it.

chunks.guide: A function literal has no name. Inside a function you can only write literals, never `func name()`.

notes.text: A function literal, stored in a variable.

chunks.guide: The variable holds a value, so assign it another literal with the same type.

exercises.title: Call a literal on the spot (IIFE)
exercises.guide: Declare a function literal and call it at once.

chunks.guide: An IIFE (immediately invoked function expression) declares a literal and calls it at once. The arguments go in the parentheses after the brace. Without them the code does not compile.

notes.text: The parentheses call the literal right away.

chunks.guide: An IIFE with a result stores what the call returns.

notes.text: fee holds the result, not the function.

exercises.title: Pass a callback
exercises.guide: Write a function that takes a function as an argument.

chunks.guide: A plain function that will be passed on as a value.
A function passed as an argument is a callback. A function that takes one is a higher-order function.

notes.text: A parameter whose type is a function type.

chunks.guide: Pass `halve` by name, then a literal written in place.

notes.text: No parentheses: passes the function, not its result.

exercises.title: A function that was never set
exercises.guide: Check a function value before you call it.

chunks.guide: The zero value of a function type is `nil`. Calling a nil function stops the program, so check first.
Run it with a nil function, then with a real one.

notes.text: No value yet, so op is nil.

exercises.title: An optional callback
exercises.guide: Make `hook` an optional callback: give it its type and guard the call.
